newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Cathay says Surabaya cargo loads low.
newsitem.headline: Cathay says Surabaya cargo loads low.

text.p: Hong Kong's Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Wednesday its air cargo loads were low out of Indonesia's second largest city of Surabaya in the face of tough competition from other centres.

Gregory Hughes, Cathay's country manager for Indonesia, told reporters potential customers in the East Java capital still preferred to ship cargo overland to the capital Jakarta or Denpasar on the island of Bali to seek competitive rates.
Jakarta is about 700 km (430 miles) west of Surabaya and Denpasar is about 300 km (186 miles) east of the city.

"Our cargo load factor has only been 30 percent," Hughes said of the twice-weekly Airbus A330-300 service non-stop to Hong Kong, adding that passenger loads on the route last year were 49 percent, slightly below the 55 percent target.

Hughes said air cargo out of Jakarta was dominated by the output of the huge footwear and textile products in West Java, while from Denpasar seafood and other fresh produce were the main cargoes. "It's very seasonal", he added.
Cathay's cargo load factors out of Denpasar and Jakarta were 70 percent and 60 percent, respectively.
However, Hughes said Surabaya had no major export industry relying on air cargo.
Studies had shown that while Surabaya was Indonesia's second largest city, the business transacted there was only nine percent of that done in the capital Jakarta, Hughes said.
Cathay Pacific flies a total of 20 non-stop flights from the Indonesian ports of Jakarta, Denpasar and Surabaya to Hong Kong every week.
